newsitem.title: USA: First Chicago NBD sees boost for municipal bonds.
newsitem.headline: First Chicago NBD sees boost for municipal bonds.

text.p: A healthy economy is boosting municipal bond volume and may also lead to upgraded ratings, the head of fixed-income investment strategy for First Chicago NBD Asset Management said this week.
In a monthly newsletter to clients, Timothy Kerr said new-issue volume is expected to increase about 10 percent this year to a total of more than $200 billion.
"This reflects a stronger economy and provides municipalities access to the debt markets for infrastructure improvements," he wrote.

Kerr added that general obligation issues should be one of the top-performing sectors of the muni market as rating agencies are expected "to reflect this strenghtening of the economy by upgrading the ratings of numerous municipal issuers."
He added that water and sewer revenue bonds should also do well mainly as a result of the reauthorization of the Safe Drinking Water Act.

Kerr cautioned investors about three sectors of the muni market -- utility issues due to deregulation, hospital issues due to the "looming overhaul of Medicare," and multi-family housing issues tied to Section 8 susidies because of anticipated restructuring of the U.S. Housing and Urban Development Department.
